data.source_title: Mass intrahospital transport of the neonatal intensive care unit: a systems-based approach to safety, efficiency, and family-centered care
data.locator: Methods, Context assessment; Results, clinical and transport variables; Discussion, full transport cycle estimates by acuity.
data.source_setting: Two planned relocations of a 24-bed intensive/high-dependency area within a 42-bed quaternary NICU at Sidra Medicine, Doha; route 120-140 m.
data.source_period: Two relocations approximately one year apart; exact event dates not stated in the article. Published 27 May 2026.
data.source_n: 34 neonates transported (17 per relocation); 33 had complete analyzed documentation (16 in relocation 1, 17 in relocation 2). Acuity subgroup denominators for the estimated cycle bands are not provided.
data.quantity: Estimated full transport cycle from preparation through team return by acuity grouping
data.unit: minutes per neonate transport cycle (approximate planning estimates)
data.source_evidence_basis: Multidisciplinary simulation and observations informed approximate full-cycle times: 30-40 minutes for ventilated neonates on multiple inotropes and inhaled nitric oxide, 20-30 minutes for stable ventilated neonates, and 15-20 minutes for stable non-invasive or room-air neonates. Actual individual departure-to-arrival medians were 4 and 6 minutes in the two relocations, a different endpoint.
data.limitations: Single-center renovation relocation; cycle bands are planning estimates without subgroup sample counts and are not distributions. Actual individual movement time excludes much of preparation and return work. Not a routine inter-hospital transport time or RWJ value.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent destination readiness, pre-transport preparation, team allocation, movement, receiving handoff, post-arrival care, and team return as separate linked tasks; vary resource needs by locally approved acuity classes without encoding clinical thresholds.

data.source_title: Mass intrahospital transport of the neonatal intensive care unit: a systems-based approach to safety, efficiency, and family-centered care
data.locator: Methods, stakeholder/work-system design; Results, transport outcomes and staff survey; Table 2.
data.source_setting: Same quaternary NICU relocations; care area had 24 intensive/high-dependency beds within a 42-bed NICU.
data.source_period: Two planned relocations approximately one year apart; exact dates not stated.
data.source_n: 34 transported neonates (33 with complete case data); 57 staff survey responses after relocation 1 and 61 after relocation 2; survey response denominator not established.
data.quantity: Observed relocation duration and staff-reported operational support needs
data.unit: minutes per relocation; staff survey response percentages and qualitative comments
data.source_evidence_basis: Two transport teams worked in parallel; the planned 255-minute total was based on 30 minutes per infant, while actual 17-infant relocations took 225 and 197 minutes. Staff feedback after the first relocation requested more nursing support, and this request persisted after the second; IT/facilities/biomedical engineering standby support addressed infrastructure problems.
data.limitations: Small, highly organized planned relocation in a quaternary NICU; voluntary survey responses and no control group. Staff positive-response percentages are not staffing adequacy measures. This is not a regular-shift nurse-to-patient ratio or RWJ staffing evidence.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Model dedicated transport teams, bedside nurse accompaniment, parallel preparation, standby technical roles, equipment readiness, huddles, and extra-support contingencies as optional resources; do not infer staffing ratios from the survey.

data.source_title: Mass intrahospital transport of the neonatal intensive care unit: a systems-based approach to safety, efficiency, and family-centered care
data.locator: Methods, parent survey; Results, Parent survey and relocation communication plan.
data.source_setting: Same NICU relocation project; parent communication, satisfaction, perceived safety, continuity, and ability to accompany infant were surveyed.
data.source_period: After each of two relocations approximately one year apart; exact dates not stated.
data.source_n: 12 parents (70% of eligible parents) responded after each relocation.
data.quantity: Parent responses on information, satisfaction, and transfer participation
data.unit: respondents per relocation; qualitative reported concern
data.source_evidence_basis: All 12 responding parents after each move reported feeling informed and satisfied with transfer and post-transfer care. The article records one concern about not being able to accompany the infant during relocation 1 and describes advance letters, face-to-face updates, invitations to accompany, and post-transfer communication.
data.limitations: Small voluntary survey with about 70% response; parent experience may not represent nonresponders. Parent accompaniment depends on route and local safety/environment constraints. Not a family-role policy for RWJ.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Include family notification, optional accompaniment, and alternate update channels as workflow needs that can compete with transport timing and route constraints; validate local policy and family preferences.
